mainTopic: The ban on new grain (חדש) on יום הנף, and how the עומר and the שתי הלחם permit new grain
overview: The amud opens with the תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: after the Temple was destroyed, new grain (חדש) is forbidden for the whole 16th of ניסן. The reason given is that people might keep eating at dawn once the Temple is rebuilt, when only the עומר can permit the grain. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that this follows רבי יהודה, who holds that the Torah itself forbids the whole day. The גמרא then reports three practices among אמוראים outside ארץ ישראל, and each one depends on how they handled the doubt about the calendar date. A new משנה teaches that the עומר permits new grain for ordinary eating and the שתי הלחם permits it for the מקדש. Offerings from new grain brought before the עומר are פסול, but those brought before the שתי הלחם are כשר. רבי יהודה בן נחמיה explains this difference to רבי טרפון, and a story follows about רבי עקיבא's warning to him. Finally רמי בר חמא asks whether the שתי הלחם can permit grain out of order. רבה tries to answer from a ברייתא proving that the עומר is barley, and the גמרא begins to reject that proof, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: The decree of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: after the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a rule that the whole day of waving the עומר is forbidden for eating new grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time the Temple was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a rule that the whole day of waving (the 16th of ניסן) is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ruling from the משנה about eating new grain after the Temple was destroyed. This is setting up the next move: the גמרא will use this ruling to ask a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no Temple, there is no עומר offering to permit the new grain. One would expect it to become allowed at dawn on the 16th, but רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade the whole day. The גמרא wants to understand why.

keyTerms.meaning: Instituted, made a rabbinic rule (a תקנה)
The day of waving the עומר, the 16th of ניסן

phrases.english: From when the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted
that the day of waving be entirely forbidden.
phrases.notes: Forbidden for eating the new grain, the topic of this פרק.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as the opening of the challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line by quoting the משנה to test the earlier claim that waiting for the עומר is only for the best way of doing the מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, eating חדש is forbidden for the entire 16th of ניסן.

steps.title: The reason: confusion once the Temple is rebuilt
steps.stepSummary: The decree exists because when the Temple is rebuilt, people may eat at dawn as they did the year before, not realizing that now the עומר is what permits the grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Because the Temple will soon be rebuilt, and people will say: 'Last year we ate as soon as the east lit up. Let us eat then now too!' They won't realize that last year there was no עומר, so dawn made it permitted, but now that there is an עומר, the עומר makes it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the decree and explains it: a fear that people will get confused once the Temple is rebuilt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a Temple, dawn of the 16th permits חדש. With a Temple, only the bringing of the עומר permits it, and that happens later in the day. If people are used to eating at dawn, they might eat before the עומר once the Temple stands, so the whole day was forbidden to break that habit.

keyTerms.meaning: The eastern sky lit up, dawn
The עומר offering permits the new grain

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two times. Without a Temple, the grain becomes permitted at dawn. With a Temple, it waits for the עומר to be brought, which happens later in the day.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Soon the Temple will be rebuilt,
and people will say: last year,
didn't we eat once the east was lit up?
Now too, let us eat!
But they would not know
that last year there was no omer,
so the lighting of the east permitted it,
but now that there is an omer, the omer permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? מְהֵרָה יִבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the decree quoted in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbid the entire day?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To stop people from eating at dawn out of habit once the Temple is rebuilt, when the עומר must permit the grain.

steps.title: Would חכמים make a decree just for the best way of doing a מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: If waiting for the עומר is only the best way of doing the מצוה and not strictly required, it makes no sense that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי would make such a strict decree to protect it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think waiting for the עומר is only for doing the מצוה in the best way, would we go and make a decree just because of a מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the decree to challenge the earlier idea that waiting for the עומר is only the best way to do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A strict decree forbidding a whole day only makes sense if eating before the עומר is a real איסור. If it were only a matter of doing the מצוה in the best way, חכמים would not make a גזירה to protect it. So the decree suggests that waiting for the עומר is truly required.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind, if you think
Only for the best way of doing the מצוה, not strictly required
Make a גזירה, a protective rabbinic decree

phrases.english: And if you think it is only for the מצוה,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier idea that waiting for the עומר is just the best way to do the מצוה, not a must.

phrases.english: would we get up and make a decree because of a מצוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לְמִצְוָה, מִשּׁוּם מִצְוָה לֵיקוּם וְלִיגְזוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the decree and its reason (steps 1-2) to attack the earlier claim.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier claim that waiting for the עומר is only for the best way of doing the מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A strict rabbinic decree only makes sense to protect a real איסור, not to protect the best way of doing a מצוה.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי followed רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling follows רבי יהודה, who holds that חדש is forbidden by Torah law based on the פסוק 'עד עצם היום הזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said this following the view of רבי יהודה, who says it is forbidden by Torah law, as it says: 'until this very day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge: the whole-day ban is not a new decree at all. It follows רבי יהודה's view that the Torah itself forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed רבן יוחנן בן זכאי invented a strict גזירה. רב נחמן בר יצחק says no: according to רבי יהודה, the Torah forbids חדש on the 16th when there is no עומר. So there is no proof from here that waiting for the עומר is a strict requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: This very day (the words of the פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the decree from a rabbinic protection into an expression of Torah law according to רבי יהודה, which removes the basis of the challenge.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
said it following the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: it is forbidden by Torah law,
as it is said: "until this very day"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a specific תנא (רבי יהודה) whose view makes the decree Torah law, not a גזירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole-day ban was a strict rabbinic decree, which would show that waiting for the עומר is required.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban follows רבי יהודה, for whom the Torah itself forbids חדש on the 16th, so it proves nothing about the earlier claim.

steps.title: How רבי יהודה reads 'עד עצם היום הזה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains the פסוק as 'until the essence of the day,' and he holds that 'עד' means up to and including, so the entire 16th is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means until the main part of the day itself, and he holds that 'until' means up to and including.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק, showing why the whole day is forbidden by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עצם היום' is read as the day itself, not just its start at dawn. Since רבי יהודה holds 'עד' includes the end point, the day itself is included in the ban. So without an עומר, חדש is only allowed after the 16th is over.

keyTerms.meaning: The essence or main part of the day, the day itself
'Until' means up to and including the end point

steps.confusionAlert: Usually 'until a day' sounds like the day itself is allowed. רבי יהודה reads 'עד' as including the day, so the whole 16th is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, when there is no עומר, the Torah forbids חדש for the entire 16th of ניסן. That is why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's whole-day ban is not just a rabbinic גזירה.

phrases.english: until the essence of the day,
phrases.notes: He means the day itself, not just the moment it starts at dawn.

phrases.english: and he holds that "until" means up to and including.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד עִיצּוּמוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם, וְקָסָבַר עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the פסוק quoted in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the derivation from the פסוק that supports the answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The entire 16th is forbidden by Torah law according to רבי יהודה (when there is no עומר).

steps.title: Doesn't רבי יהודה argue with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 4. The משנה itself shows רבי יהודה disagreeing with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבן יוחנן בן זכאי really agree with רבי יהודה? Doesn't רבי יהודה argue with him? We learned in the משנה: after the Temple was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a rule that the whole day of waving the עומר is forbidden. רבי יהודה said: but isn't it forbidden by Torah law, since the פסוק says 'until this very day'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי follows רבי יהודה. It quotes the full משנה, where רבי יהודה seems to argue with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rules like רבי יהודה. But in the משנה, רבי יהודה reacts with 'והלא', meaning 'but isn't it already Torah law?' That sounds like a disagreement, not agreement.

keyTerms.meaning: He clearly disagrees (the doubled verb adds emphasis)
The day the עומר is waved, the 16th of ניסן
'But isn't it...?', a pushback that something is already true

phrases.english: And does he hold like him?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, and 'him' is רבי יהודה, from Step 4.

phrases.english: But he clearly disagrees with him!
As we learned: from when the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted
that the day of waving should be entirely forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מִן הַתּוֹרָה הוּא אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: But isn't it forbidden by Torah law,
as it is written: 'Until this very day'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ? וְהָא מִיפְלָג פְּלִיג עֲלֵיהּ!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer from Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, רבי יהודה pushes back against רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling, so the two cannot share one view.

steps.title: רבי יהודה misunderstood רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה thought the decree was rabbinic. In truth, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant it as Torah law, so they really agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה who is mistaken. He thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant a rabbinic rule, but that is not so. He meant it as Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no real argument. רבי יהודה simply misread what רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה objected because he thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was adding a rabbinic decree. The גמרא says רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was stating the Torah law, the same as רבי יהודה. So the objection came from a misunderstanding, not from a different opinion.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda who is mistaken.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא סָבַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: He thought that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
is speaking of rabbinic law.
But it is not so; he is speaking of Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּקָא טָעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the dispute as a misunderstanding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי argue about whether the prohibition is Torah or rabbinic
steps.terutzMaskana: Both hold it is Torah law; רבי יהודה only thought רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant a rabbinic rule

steps.title: But the משנה says he 'instituted'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'התקין' sounds like a new rabbinic decree, which goes against the answer of Step 7.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says he 'instituted'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 7 using one word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'התקין' normally means the חכמים created a new rule. If רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was only stating Torah law, why would the משנה say he 'instituted' something?

keyTerms.meaning: Instituted, made a תקנה (normally a rabbinic enactment)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'instituted'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״הִתְקִין״ קָתָנֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'התקין' signals a rabbinic decree, not a statement of Torah law.

steps.title: 'Instituted' means he explained the פסוק and set up the practice
steps.stepSummary: 'התקין' here means רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explained the פסוק and then set the practice for the public.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'instituted' mean? He explained the פסוק and then established the practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word 'התקין' so that it fits a Torah-law prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי did not create a new law. He explained what the פסוק 'עד עצם היום הזה' requires and made sure the people acted on it. That public setup is what the משנה calls 'התקין'. This closes the question that began in Step 3.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבי יהודה agree: חדש is forbidden all of the 16th by Torah law. 'התקין' means he explained the פסוק and set up a public practice. It was not a new rabbinic decree.

phrases.english: What does 'instituted' mean?
He explained the verse and instituted the practice.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״הִתְקִין״? דָּרַשׁ וְהִתְקִין.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzMaskana: 'התקין' means he explained the Torah law and set up public practice based on it

steps.title: רב פפא and רב הונא eat חדש on the night after the 16th
steps.stepSummary: These אמוראים ate חדש on the night of the 17th. They held חדש outside ארץ ישראל is rabbinic, so they did not worry about doubt over the date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע ate new grain on the night after the 16th, going into the 17th. They held that חדש outside ארץ ישראל is rabbinic, and we are not concerned about the doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: what אמוראים actually did about eating חדש. Here it reports the practice of רב פפא and רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside ארץ ישראל there was doubt about the exact date, so the day called the 16th might really have been the 15th. Since they held חדש there is only rabbinic, they were lenient on the doubt. They ate as soon as their 16th ended.

keyTerms.meaning: New grain, forbidden until the עומר

steps.confusionAlert: The 'doubt' here is not about the law of חדש. It is about the calendar: people outside ארץ ישראל could not be sure which day ניסן began. So the day they called the 16th might really have been the 15th.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: אָכְלִי חָדָשׁ בְּאוּרְתָּא דְּשִׁיתְּסַר נַגְהֵי שִׁבְסַר,
phrases.english: ate new grain on the evening ending the sixteenth, leading into the seventeenth.
They hold: new grain outside the Land is rabbinic,
and we are not concerned about the doubt.
phrases.notes: The doubt is whether their 16th was really the 15th, since they weren't sure of the date.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָכְלִי חָדָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory of יום הנף to actual practice outside ארץ ישראל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since חדש outside ארץ ישראל is rabbinic, one may eat it on the night after the 16th, without worrying about doubt over the date.

steps.title: The חכמים of רב אשי's study hall wait until the morning of the 17th
steps.stepSummary: They held חדש outside ארץ ישראל is Torah law, so they took the doubt over the date into account and waited until the morning of the 17th.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים of רב אשי's study hall ate only on the morning of the 17th. They held that חדש outside ארץ ישראל is Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, stricter practice that is the opposite of Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because they held the prohibition is from the Torah, they were strict about the doubt. Their 16th might really have been the 15th, so they waited until the morning of the 17th. The whole difference between the two practices is whether חדש in חוצה לארץ is דרבנן or דאורייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two practices show a basic rule: with a Torah prohibition we are strict about a doubt, and with a rabbinic one we may be lenient.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא and רב הונא held חדש in חוצה לארץ is rabbinic, so they ignored the date doubt and ate on the night after the 16th. The חכמים of רב אשי's study hall held it is Torah law, so they waited until the morning of the 17th.

phrases.english: And the Sages of Rav Ashi's study hall
ate on the morning of the seventeenth.
They hold: new grain outside the Land is Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי אָכְלִי בְּצַפְרָא דְּשִׁבְסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite practice to Step 10, based on the opposite view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since חדש outside ארץ ישראל is Torah law, the doubt over the date must be taken into account, and one waits until the morning of the 17th.

steps.title: The decree of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי does not cover a doubtful day
steps.stepSummary: The אמוראים who ate on the morning of the 17th held that the all-day ban of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is only rabbinic, so it was never made for a day that is only possibly the 16th.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was talking about a rabbinic law. When he made his decree for the day of waving, he did not make it for a day that is only a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question. If the 17th might really be the 16th, how could these אמוראים eat on its morning, when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade the whole 16th?
steps.deeperAnalysis: These אמוראים hold that by Torah law חדש becomes permitted at dawn of the 16th. Only the all-day ban is a rabbinic decree. The decree was made for the real יום הנף, not for a day that is only possibly the 16th, so on the morning of the 17th they could eat.

keyTerms.meaning: by rabbinic law, not Torah law
the day of waving the עומר, the 16th of ניסן
a doubt; here, a day whose real date is uncertain

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Steps 7–9. There, according to רבי יהודה, the decree was really Torah law. Here these אמוראים read the all-day ban of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי as rabbinic, even though they hold חדש outside ארץ ישראל is Torah law.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מִדְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: And Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was speaking of a rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: This answers a question the גמרא leaves unsaid: if the 17th might be the 16th, how could they eat that morning?

phrases.english: and when he instituted it for the day of waving,
for a doubtful day he did not institute it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מִדְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the practice in Step 11 against an implied challenge from the decree of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the decree: it is rabbinic and does not apply to a doubtful day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The all-day ban should forbid eating on the 17th, since the 17th might really be the 16th.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbinic decree covers only the actual יום הנף, not a doubtful day, so eating on the morning of the 17th is allowed.

steps.title: רבינא's father waited until the night after the 17th
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports in his mother's name that his father ate חדש only from the night after the 17th, because he held like רבי יהודה and worried about the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: My mother told me that your father would eat new grain only on the night after the 17th, going into the 18th. This was because he held like רבי יהודה and he worried about the doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third practice, stricter than the ones before. רבינא's father waited until the 18th began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יהודה, he held that the all-day ban on the 16th is Torah law. Since the 17th might really be the 16th, the whole 17th could be forbidden by Torah law. So he waited until that night, when the doubtful day was fully over.

keyTerms.meaning: new grain of this year, forbidden until the עומר
leading into, the night before (a day)

steps.whatToRemember: Three practices: (1) eat on the night of the 17th, since חדש is rabbinic; (2) eat on the morning of the 17th, since it is Torah law but the all-day decree is rabbinic; (3) wait until the night after the 17th, like רבי יהודה, since the all-day ban is Torah law and the date is in doubt.

phrases.english: Ravina said: My mother told me:
Your father would not eat new grain
except on the evening at the end of the seventeenth, leading into the eighteenth,
because he held like Rabbi Yehuda,
and he was concerned about the doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אָמְרָה לִי אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter practice after Steps 10–12, based on the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who holds like רבי יהודה and worries about the doubt over the date waits until the night after the 17th to eat חדש.

steps.title: משנה: what the עומר and the שתי הלחם permit
steps.stepSummary: The עומר permits new grain for the country, and the שתי הלחם permit it for the מקדש. Offerings from new grain brought before the עומר are פסול, but those brought before the שתי הלחם are כשר after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עומר would permit new grain in the country, and the שתי הלחם would permit it in the מקדש. One may not bring מנחות, ביכורים, or the מנחה that comes with an animal offering before the עומר. If he did, it is פסול. Before the שתי הלחם he should not bring them, but if he did, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets two stages for new grain: the עומר for ordinary eating, and the שתי הלחם for use in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the עומר, new grain is fully forbidden, so an offering made from it is פסול. After the עומר but before the שתי הלחם, one should not bring it, but if he did, it still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: the barley offering on the 16th of ניסן that permits new grain
the two wheat loaves offered on שבועות
the country, everywhere outside the מקדש
first fruits brought to the מקדש
the flour offering that comes along with an animal sacrifice

steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between פסול before the עומר and כשר before the שתי הלחם is what the גמרא now sets out to explain.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The omer would permit new grain in the country,
and the two loaves would permit it in the Temple.
One may not bring meal offerings, or first fruits,
or the meal offering of an animal, before the omer;
phrases.notes: This is the flour offering brought together with an animal sacrifice and its wine.

phrases.english: if he brought them, they are unfit.
Before the two loaves he should not bring them,
but if he brought them, they are fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָעוֹמֶר הָיָה מַתִּיר בַּמְּדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New-grain offerings before the עומר are פסול. Before the שתי הלחם they should not be brought, but are כשר if brought.

steps.title: רבי טרפון asks why before the עומר differs from before the שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון finds the משנה's distinction difficult: why is an offering brought before the עומר פסול, but one brought before the שתי הלחם כשר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון sat and found it difficult: what is the difference between before the עומר and before the שתי הלחם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by challenging the משנה's distinction. It is setting up the search for a reason in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the new grain has not yet been permitted for its use, either in the country or in the מקדש. So why should the outcome differ, פסול in one case and כשר in the other? רבי טרפון wants the source or logic behind the difference.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Tarfon sat
and found it difficult:
What is the difference between before the omer
and before the two loaves?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְקָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction set out in the משנה in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that before the עומר it is פסול, but before the שתי הלחם it is כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both are cases of new grain that has not yet been permitted, so they seem to deserve the same outcome.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן נחמיה explains the difference
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן נחמיה answers רבי טרפון: before the עומר new grain is forbidden to everyone, but before the שתי הלחם it is already allowed to ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בר נחמיה said before him: No! Before the עומר, the new grain was not yet allowed to anyone. Before the שתי הלחם, it was already allowed to ordinary people. So you cannot treat the two cases the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן נחמיה answers the question רבי טרפון asked in step 15. He shows why the two cases in the משנה really are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the עומר, new grain is completely forbidden, even to a regular person, so an offering made from it is פסול. After the עומר it is already allowed for regular people. It is only still waiting to be allowed for the מקדש, so an offering brought before the שתי הלחם is כשר after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: No, if you said: a formula for rejecting a comparison by pointing out a difference
its general ban was already lifted
an ordinary person, as opposed to the מקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that a thing already allowed to ordinary people is treated more leniently, is the reasoning רב נחמן בר יצחק builds on in steps 19 to 21.

phrases.english: Yehuda bar Nechemya said before him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking before רבי טרפון, answering his question from the last step.

phrases.english: No! If you said this about an offering brought before the עומר,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ אֵצֶל הֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: that is because its general ban had not been lifted even for an ordinary person,
will you say the same about one brought before the two loaves,
when its general ban was already lifted for an ordinary person?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ קוֹדֶם לָעוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טרפון's question from step 15
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases involve new grain that is not yet allowed for the offering, so both should be פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before the שתי הלחם the grain is already allowed to ordinary people, so it is less forbidden and the offering is כשר after the fact.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא rebukes Yehuda for being pleased
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון goes silent, רבי יהודה בן נחמיה looks happy, and רבי עקיבא warns him that being glad to silence an elder will cost him long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון was silent. רבי יהודה בן נחמיה's face lit up. רבי עקיבא said to him: יהודה, are you glowing because you answered an elder? I would be surprised if you live long.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a story. רבי טרפון has no reply, רבי יהודה בן נחמיה is visibly pleased, and רבי עקיבא rebukes him for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer itself was correct. The problem was that he looked happy that he had beaten an older תלמיד חכם. רבי עקיבא treats that as a lack of respect serious enough to shorten a person's life.

keyTerms.meaning: he was silent, meaning he had no reply
his face lit up with pleasure
an elder, an older Torah scholar

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon was silent,

phrases.aramaic: צָהֲבוּ פָּנָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן נְחֶמְיָה,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda ben Nechemya's face lit up.
Rabbi Akiva said to him:
Yehuda, your face lit up
because you answered an elder?
I would be surprised if you live long.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁתַק רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what happened after רבי יהודה בן נחמיה's answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking pleasure in silencing an elder is a serious failing, and רבי עקיבא warns that it may cost long life.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן נחמיה died within weeks
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר אלעאי reports that the incident was about two weeks before פסח, and by שבועות רבי יהודה בן נחמיה had already died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי said: That happened about two weeks before פסח. When I came up for שבועות, I asked where יהודה בן נחמיה was. They told me he had died.
steps.whatsHappening: An eyewitness finishes the story. רבי עקיבא's warning came true within a few weeks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling us the exact timing, from two weeks before פסח until שבועות, shows how quickly it happened. This drives home how seriously we must treat respect for an elder.

keyTerms.meaning: about half a month before פסח

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה and the story go together: רבי יהודה בן נחמיה's logic was right, but being happy that he had silenced an elder was treated with great severity.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Ilai said:
That time was about half a month before Pesach.
When I went up for Shavuos,
I asked about him:
Where is Yehuda ben Nechemya?
And they told me: He passed away and is gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story and shows רבי עקיבא's warning came true
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן נחמיה died between פסח and שבועות, as רבי עקיבא had warned.

steps.title: Libations from first fruits before the עומר are valid
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that according to רבי יהודה בן נחמיה, נסכים from ביכורים brought before the עומר are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: According to יהודה בן נחמיה, libations from first fruits that someone brought before the עומר are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the halacha. רב נחמן בר יצחק applies רבי יהודה בן נחמיה's reasoning to a new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on new produce before the עומר applies only to grain, so fruit was never forbidden to an ordinary person. If grain that is already allowed to ordinary people can be offered, then fruit that was never forbidden can also be offered, even before the עומר.

keyTerms.meaning: libations, the wine poured on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
According to the words of Yehuda ben Nechemya,
libations from first fruits
phrases.notes: This is fruit, not grain, and the new-grain ban only covers grain. So this was never forbidden to anyone.

phrases.english: that someone offered before the עומר are valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לְדִבְרֵי יְהוּדָה בֶּן נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story to apply step 16's reasoning to a new case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה בן נחמיה, נסכים from ביכורים offered before the עומר are כשר.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן בר יצחק needed to say this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק: why say something so obvious? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If grain that was once forbidden can be offered, then fruit that was never forbidden should surely be fine too. So the statement seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: that's obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 19 teaches anything new
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement in step 19
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fruit that was never forbidden is obviously no worse than grain that is already allowed, so there is no need to say it.

steps.title: We might have thought only a lifted ban counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one might think the leniency applies only where a ban was lifted, so רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches that it applies all the more where there was never a ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there, the offering is valid because a ban was lifted for ordinary people. But here, where no ban was lifted, it is not valid. So he teaches us: all the more so here, where it was never forbidden at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement is needed. Someone could have made a mistake about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that 'already allowed to ordinary people' was a special requirement, so fruit, which never went through a lifted ban, would not count. רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches that the real point is how forbidden the item is. Something never forbidden is even better.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said: introduces a wrong assumption the teaching rules out

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה בן נחמיה, what matters is how forbidden the item is. Grain that is already allowed to ordinary people is כשר after the fact, and fruit that was never forbidden is כשר all the more so.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּהוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ אֵצֶל הֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: it is only there that it is valid, since its general ban was lifted for an ordinary person,
phrases.notes: There means the grain offering brought after the עומר but before the שתי הלחם.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלֹא הוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ – לָא.
phrases.english: but here, where no general ban was lifted, it is not valid.
So he teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן הָכָא, דְּלָא אִיתְּסַר כְּלָל.
phrases.english: all the more so here, where it was never forbidden at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָתָם הוּא דְּהוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ אֵצֶל הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a possible mistake to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only something whose ban was lifted counts, so fruit, which never had a lifted ban, would be פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Something never forbidden is כשר all the more so.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's question: do the שתי הלחם permit grain out of order?
steps.stepSummary: After a memory aid for the coming topics, רמי בר חמא asks whether the שתי הלחם can permit new grain when it comes out of its usual order.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: order, sprouting, dung, elephant.) רמי בר חמא asked: do the שתי הלחם permit new grain even when they come out of their order?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רמי בר חמא asks a question about the order in which the עומר and the שתי הלחם permit new grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the עומר comes first, on פסח, and permits new grain for everyday eating. The שתי הלחם comes later, on שבועות, and permits new grain for use in the מקדש. רמי בר חמא asks what happens when, for a certain batch of grain, this order is flipped.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid. These are short code words that help you remember the upcoming topics.
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות. They permit new grain to be used in the מקדש.

phrases.english: (Order, sprouting, dung of, elephant: a memory aid.)
phrases.notes: These code words help you remember the next few discussions. Some versions leave this line out, which is why it's in round brackets.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
The two loaves, what is the law
as to whether they permit when out of their order?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the discussion of רבי יהודה בן נחמיה and נסכים in steps 19-21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the permission given by the שתי הלחם and the עומר depends on their coming in the usual order.

steps.title: Defining the case and laying out both sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the case: grain planted between the עומר and שבועות, so that the שתי הלחם comes before the next עומר. Does the permission work only in order, or out of order too?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Grain was planted between the עומר and the שתי הלחם. Then the שתי הלחם passed over it first, and only afterward the next year's עומר. What is the law? Do they permit only in their order and not out of order? Or perhaps they permit even out of order?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רמי בר חמא's question looks like in real life. Then it states the two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain planted after this year's עומר was not permitted by that עומר. So the first offering to pass over it is the שתי הלחם, and the next year's עומר only comes later. The question is whether the order matters: is grain permitted only when the עומר comes first, or does it work either way?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? It asks for the exact situation.
Passed over them, meaning the offering happened while this grain was growing.
Or perhaps. It introduces the other side of the question.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
For example, where they planted it
between the עומר and the two loaves,
and the two loaves and then the עומר passed over them.
phrases.notes: He means the next year's עומר, which only comes after this שבועות.

phrases.english: What is the law?
In their order they permit,
but out of their order they do not permit?
Or perhaps
out of their order they also permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the case behind רמי בר חמא's question and states its two sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the עומר and שתי הלחם permission need the usual order, or does it work in reverse order too?

steps.title: רבה starts a proof from a ברייתא about the עומר
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings a ברייתא saying the פסוק of מנחת ביכורים refers to the עומר, which comes from barley. The ברייתא then asks how we know it is barley and not wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Come and hear. "And if you bring a מנחת ביכורים": the פסוק is speaking about the מנחת העומר. What grain is it brought from? From barley. Do you say from barley, or maybe it is only from wheat?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins bringing a source to answer רמי בר חמא's question. This step only sets up the ברייתא. The actual proof is not finished yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first says which offering the פסוק is talking about: the עומר. It then states that the עומר is made from barley. Next it asks how we know it is not wheat. That question sets up the proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering of first grain. Here it means the עומר.

phrases.english: Rabba said: Come and hear,
"And if you bring a meal offering of first fruits":
the verse is speaking of the עומר meal offering.
From what is it brought?
From barley.
Do you say from barley,
or is it perhaps only from wheat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an attempt to settle רמי בר חמא's question from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רמי בר חמא's question about the order of the עומר and the שתי הלחם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 2:14 about the מנחת העומר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: "אביב" means barley, as in Egypt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר compares the word "אביב" in the story of Egypt with "אביב" said about the עומר for all generations. In Egypt it meant barley, so here it means barley too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: "אביב" is said about Egypt, and "אביב" is said for all generations. Just as the "אביב" said about Egypt is barley, so too the "אביב" said for all generations is barley.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר answers the question of the last step. He proves the עומר is barley by comparing two uses of the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the plague of hail, the פסוק says the barley was "אביב" (in ripe ears), while the wheat was not yet ripe. Since the same word appears about the עומר, רבי אליעזר learns that the עומר is also barley. רבה's proof for רמי בר חמא's question continues after this.

keyTerms.meaning: For all generations. Here it means the lasting מצוה of the עומר.
Just as ... so too. This is the pattern for comparing two cases.
Learning the meaning of one פסוק from the same word in another פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"In the ear" is stated regarding Egypt,
phrases.notes: שמות 9:31, about the plague of hail.

phrases.english: and "in the ear" is stated for all generations.
phrases.notes: This is the עומר פסוק, ויקרא 2:14.

phrases.english: Just as the "in the ear" stated regarding Egypt is barley,
so too the "in the ear" stated for all generations is barley.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר ״אָבִיב״ בְּמִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 24: how we know the עומר is barley and not wheat.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עומר is barley, learned from the shared word "אביב" in the plague of hail in Egypt.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the community must also have a barley obligation
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא argues from a parallel. An individual brings required offerings from both wheat and barley, and the community brings from wheat. So the community must also bring something from barley, and that can only be the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: We find that an individual brings his required offering from wheat, and also his required offering from barley. The community brings its required offering from wheat, so it should also bring its required offering from barley. If you say the עומר comes from wheat, we would never find the community bringing a required offering from barley.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second proof, from רבי עקיבא, that the עומר is barley. He builds a parallel between the individual and the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual has required מנחות of both wheat and barley. The community already has a wheat offering, the שתי הלחם. To keep the parallel, the community needs a barley offering too, and the only candidate is the עומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The community, the whole Jewish people

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: מָצִינוּ יָחִיד שֶׁמֵּבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִן הַחִיטִּין,
phrases.english: We found an individual who brings his obligation from wheat,
and his obligation from barley.
And the community, who bring their obligation from wheat,
should bring their obligation from barley,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בָּא מִן הַחִיטִּין –
phrases.english: and if you say it comes from wheat,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָצִינוּ צִיבּוּר שֶׁמֵּבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִין.
phrases.english: we have not found a community that brings its obligation from barley.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מָצִינוּ יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proof, from רבי עקיבא, beside רבי אליעזר's גזירה שוה from 'אביב'
steps.raayaObject: That the עומר is brought from barley
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel between an individual's offerings and the community's offerings

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's second proof: otherwise the two loaves are not first fruits
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא adds another proof. If the עומר were wheat, it would come before the שתי הלחם, and then the שתי הלחם could not be called 'ביכורים', the first of the new crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: If you say the עומר comes from wheat, then the שתי הלחם would not be 'first fruits'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives one more reason the עומר must be barley. This is the line רבה will use to answer רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls the שתי הלחם 'ביכורים', the first offering from the new wheat. If the עומר on פסח were also wheat, it would be the first new-wheat offering, and the שתי הלחם would come second. So the עומר must be barley.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits, the first offering from the new crop
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

steps.whyThisMatters: רבה builds his answer to רמי בר חמא directly on this argument in the next step.

phrases.english: Alternatively:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר עוֹמֶר בָּא מִן הַחִיטִּין –
phrases.english: if you say the omer comes from wheat,
the two loaves are not "first fruits."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר עוֹמֶר בָּא מִן הַחִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An additional proof from רבי עקיבא for the same point
steps.raayaObject: That the עומר is brought from barley
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק calling the שתי הלחם 'ביכורים'

steps.title: רבה: out-of-order two loaves do not permit
steps.stepSummary: רבה shows how this answers רמי בר חמא. Suppose שתי הלחם out of order could permit new grain. Then even with a wheat עומר, there would be grain for which the שתי הלחם came first. Since רבי עקיבא says they would not be ביכורים, out-of-order שתי הלחם must not permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were true that the שתי הלחם permit new grain even out of order, you could find a case where the שתי הלחם are still ביכורים even with a wheat עומר: the עומר is brought from wheat that took root before the שתי הלחם (last year's) but after last year's עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה uses רבי עקיבא's last proof to answer רמי בר חמא's question from Step 22. He shows that if out-of-order permission worked, רבי עקיבא's argument would fall apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take wheat that took root after last year's עומר but before last year's שתי הלחם. For that wheat, last year's שתי הלחם passed over it first, out of order. If that could permit it, this wheat would already count as permitted, so a wheat עומר brought from it this year would not be the first of the new crop, and this year's שתי הלחם (step 29) could still be ביכורים. Since רבי עקיבא says a wheat עומר would stop the שתי הלחם from being ביכורים, out-of-order שתי הלחם must not permit.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה tries to answer רמי בר חמא from רבי עקיבא: the שתי הלחם permit new grain only in their usual order, after the עומר. In step 30 the גמרא begins to reject this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the עומר really is wheat. He imagines what would follow if out-of-order permission worked, and shows that this clashes with רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: And if it is so that the two loaves
permit even when not in their order,
phrases.notes: This is רמי בר חמא's question from earlier.

phrases.english: you find it where one sacrifices the omer
from those grains that took root before the two loaves,
and after the omer of last year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא דִּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם שֶׁלֹּא כְּסִדְרָן שַׁרְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא's second proof to answer רמי בר חמא's question
steps.raayaObject: That שתי הלחם brought out of order do not permit new grain
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's claim that a wheat עומר would stop the שתי הלחם from being ביכורים

steps.title: רבה names the grain the שתי הלחם would come from
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his proof. If out-of-order שתי הלחם could permit, they could be brought from wheat that took root after last year's שתי הלחם and before this year's עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the two loaves could be brought from that grain which took root before this year's עומר and after last year's two loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes the proof he started in step 28. He points to the exact grain the שתי הלחם would be brought from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take wheat that took root in the window between last year's שתי הלחם and this year's עומר. For that wheat, the שתי הלחם would still be the first offering of the new crop, even with a wheat עומר. רבי עקיבא says a wheat עומר would stop the שתי הלחם from being ביכורים, so he must hold that out-of-order שתי הלחם do not permit grain.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves of wheat brought on שבועות, called ביכורים, the first of the new crop

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's proof: if out-of-order שתי הלחם could permit grain, they could be ביכורים even with a wheat עומר. רבי עקיבא says they could not, so out-of-order שתי הלחם do not permit. The next step begins to push back on this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different years here. The grain took root after LAST year's שתי הלחם but before THIS year's עומר. That window is what lets the שתי הלחם be first for this grain.

phrases.english: And the two loaves [could be brought] from those [grains]
that took root before this year's עומר
and after last year's two loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם מֵהָנָךְ דְּאַשְׁרוּשׁ קוֹדֶם לָעוֹמֶר דְּהַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the sentence and proof that רבה began in step 28
steps.raayaObject: That שתי הלחם brought out of order do not permit new grain (answering רמי בר חמא)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's argument in the ברייתא that a wheat עומר would stop the שתי הלחם from being ביכורים

steps.title: The גמרא starts to push back on רבה's proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its rejection of רבה's proof with 'מי סברת', 'Do you hold...'. The rest of the rejection comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you hold...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It begins to say that רבה's proof does not work, and the explanation follows right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מי סברת' means 'do you think'. It signals that the proof rests on an assumption the גמרא is about to question. Here it is the start of a rejection of רבה's reading of רבי עקיבא, not a real question looking for information.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think / do you hold? This phrase opens a challenge to an assumption

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished here. The rest of the rejection continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Do you hold

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to reject the proof רבה just finished
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה's proof from רבי עקיבא about out-of-order שתי הלחם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated. The flaw is spelled out in the continuation.
